name: Five and Soccer
source: written 8 Nov 2026 from his own brief, revised the same day: the big upper day moved off the morning after soccer, which is now a short day and stretching.

constraints.soccer: Wednesday, and it is a leg session whether or not it is written down. Nothing heavy on Tuesday, and Thursday is short and soft - no loaded work the day after a match.
constraints.lowerback: hinge is loaded but never rounded - the set ends the rep the back changes shape, not the rep after
constraints.knee: the knee circuit runs before both leg days, and no jumping on the day after soccer
constraints.shortdays: 10 to 15 minutes means one movement and a clock. A short day that grows into a session is a short day nobody does.

goals: Legs twice a week, once heavy and once for volume
One upper day that earns its 45 minutes: load first, volume after, and far from the match
Two short days that are a push, and one that is recovery with a push attached
Fundamentals only, so every session is a movement worth owning

d1.name: Legs · Load
d1.why: Monday, two days clear of Wednesday's match, which is the only slot in the week where heavy legs do not borrow from something else. Low reps, long rests, and the set ends when the shape does.

blocks.name: Knee armour
blocks.note: 2 rounds, controlled. This is the reason both leg days are repeatable.

items.note: Ankles first. A stiff ankle is a knee problem.

blocks.name: A · Back Squat
blocks.note: 4 × 5, rest 150s. The heaviest thing in the week. Ramp to it, do not start there.

items.note: Stop 1 short. Depth you can repeat beats depth you can reach once.

blocks.name: B · Romanian Deadlift
blocks.note: 3 × 6, rest 120s. Load the hinge while the back is fresh.

items.note: Hips back, bar on the legs. The set ends the rep the back rounds.

blocks.name: C · Bulgarian Split Squat
blocks.note: 3 × 8 each side, rest 90s. One leg at a time, which is how you actually play.

items.note: Start at 40 lb, the number from your survey.

blocks.name: Suitcase Carry
blocks.note: 3 rounds, 40s per side, 45s between. The cheapest lower-back insurance there is.

items.note: One bell. Do not let the ribs tip.

d2.name: Short · The Burpee Hundred
d2.why: Tuesday, the day after heavy legs and the day before the match, so this is deliberately not a leg session. One movement, a clock, and a number to beat. Your 8:34 is the thing to chase.

blocks.name: Loosen
blocks.note: Straight through, once. Two minutes, not five.

blocks.name: 100 Burpees for time
blocks.note: 100 reps, broken however you like, clock running from the first one. Write the time down. Best so far: 8:34. Alternate weeks with the pull-up ladder: minute 1 is 1 rep, minute 2 is 2, until a minute you cannot finish.

items.note: Sets of 10 held together beat sets of 20 that fall apart. Step back if the knee says so.

d3.name: Short · Push and unwind
d3.why: Thursday, the morning after the match. Everything here is deliberately small: one upper movement so the day still counts for something, then ten minutes of putting the hips, ankles and back back where they were before ninety minutes of soccer moved them. Nothing loaded, nothing for the legs.

blocks.name: Push-ups, every minute
blocks.note: 6 minutes. 12 push-ups on the top of each minute, rest the remainder. If 12 stops being hard, make it 15, not 7 minutes.

items.note: Chest to the floor. If the last minute breaks form, drop to 10 and keep the shape.

blocks.name: Unwind the match
blocks.note: 2 rounds, no rest, breathe through the holds. This is the half of the day that matters.

items.note: Where ninety minutes of running puts everything. Tuck the tailbone or you are just arching your back.
Slow. The lower back earned it.

d4.name: Legs · Reps
d4.why: Friday, two days after the match and two days before the next one. Nothing on this day is heavy. Long sets, short rests, and the legs get the volume that the Monday session cannot afford to give them.

blocks.name: Knee armour
blocks.note: 2 rounds. The same circuit as Monday, and just as non-optional.

blocks.name: A · Goblet Squat
blocks.note: 4 × 15, rest 60s. Light enough that the fifteenth rep looks like the first.

items.note: Pause at the bottom. This is where the range is bought.

blocks.name: B · Single-Leg RDL
blocks.note: 3 × 12 each side, rest 60s. Alternating sides is the rest.

items.note: Thighs wherever the knee is happy.

d5.name: Upper · Load then volume
d5.why: Saturday. The only full upper session in the week, and it sits here because it is the one day with a clear run at it: two days after the match, a rest day behind it, and no legs involved either way. It does both jobs in the order that works - the heaviest pull and press first while you are fresh, then the same patterns again for reps once the strength work is banked.

blocks.name: Shoulders, wrists and grip
blocks.note: Straight through. The wrists matter because dips load them cold.

blocks.name: A · Weighted Chin-Up
blocks.note: 4 × 5, rest 150s. Heaviest pull of the week, done first.

items.note: A dumbbell between the feet. Full hang at the bottom, every rep.
Stop 1 short. Elbows where the shoulder likes them.

blocks.name: C · Dip + Single-Arm Row
blocks.note: C1 into C2, no rest, then 75s. The volume half: same patterns, lighter, more reps.

items.note: superset C2 · chest on the bench
